heard: A classified military mirror is about to outscan the Hubble telescope. In 2012, the National Reconnaissance Office surprised NASA by donating two 2.4-meter surveillance mirrors. NASA's first chief of astronomy, Nancy Grace Roman, inspired the agency to repurpose one for a new mission. Engineers adapted this reconnaissance hardware into a flagship observatory to solve the mysteries of dark energy. On August 30, 2026, a SpaceX Falcon Heavy will carry this former spy tool to a point 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope matches Hubble's resolution, but captures an area 100 times larger. It is expected to scan more of the sky in five years than Hubble did in over 30. That incredible survey power stems entirely from recycling top-secret military hardware.
